children: A Bengaluru-based advertising executive has accused an Urban Company service professional of stealing his wife's wedding ring during a home cleaning appointment, sparking debate online about accountability and customer support in the rapidly growing home-services sector.

Shubham Mazumdar shared the allegation in a LinkedIn post that has attracted significant attention, claiming the ring was stolen by a worker assigned through Urban Company's InstaHelp cleaning service.
According to Mazumdar, he had booked an InstaHelp cleaning session under the company's premium "Gold Expert" category when the ring allegedly went missing.
"Urban Company sent a thief into my home who stole my wife's wedding ring," he wrote.
Mazumdar said he immediately reported the matter through the app and was informed by customer support that the company had a recovery team and would require four to five days to investigate.
He, however, claimed little progress was made in the days that followed.
"A day went by with nothing," he wrote, adding that he later contacted the company's grievance officer seeking a named point of contact and details of the service professional.
According to Mazumdar, he received what he described as a template response.
'I wasn't going to wait'
Mazumdar said customer support subsequently advised him to file a police complaint. But, by that point he had already approached law enforcement.
"Good thing I'd already filed it. I'd read online how they deal with theft, so I wasn't going to wait on them," he wrote.
The most striking part of the account involved the alleged recovery of the jewellery.
According to Mazumdar, police eventually traced and recovered the ring from a location roughly 100 kilometres outside Bengaluru.
"The police got the ring back from about 100 km outside Bangalore. I had to book an intercity Uber so they could go and recover it," he claimed.
Frustration over automated messages

Mazumdar's post included screenshots showing automated messages from Urban Company requesting feedback on the completed service. One screenshot appeared to show the company sending a service-rating request shortly after the incident.
"Then came an automated SMS from Urban Company: 'Please rate and review your service'," Mazumdar wrote. "Heights of automated customer experience."
Urban Company's response

Responding publicly under the LinkedIn post, Urban Company said: "Hi Shubham, We apologise for the inconvenience caused and regret the experience you had with our service. Kindly share your registered contact number via DM so that we can look into the matter and assist you further."
The response, however, drew a sharp rebuttal from Mazumdar, who questioned why the company was seeking details that he believed were already available through the ongoing support tickets.
"How about let me draft an empathetic reply which you should have done here," he wrote.
Debate erupts online
The post triggered a wider debate about consumer responsibility, service-provider accountability and trust in app-based home services.
Some users expressed sympathy and criticised Urban Company's handling of the issue.
"A customer doing what the company's CX team should be doing," one commenter wrote. Another claimed to have experienced similar incidents and alleged that the company's response had been inadequate.
Others argued customers should take greater precautions with valuables during home-service visits.

One user commented: "Getting a branded maid doesn't mean that you keep your gold in front of her." Another suggested that incidents of alleged theft could damage consumer trust in emerging on-demand services such as Urban Company and similar startups.

title: Bengaluru man says Urban Company professional stole wife's gold ring. Company responds
